commands.description: Answer an aggregate patent question with agent-written SQL through `patstat_query` (CLI: `flowleap patstat query "<sql>" --question "<question>"`) under the deterministic gate — the one-retry loop. Toyota leads the core all-solid-state field, with Samsung, Panasonic, LG and the Hyundai-Kia group close behind. Japan and Korea own the technology, while China is the largest filing destination. Source: PATSTAT 2026 Spring edition, applicant counts by patent family for filings since 2016.

**Inorganic solid electrolytes (CPC H01M10/0562, the core all-solid-state class, 12,909 families)**

| Rank | Applicant | Families since 2016 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Toyota | 610 |
| 2 | Panasonic | 507 |
| 3 | Samsung SDI | 463 |
| 4 | LG Energy Solution | 313 |
| 5 | Hyundai | 268 |
| 6 | Samsung Electronics | 267 |
| 7 | Kia | 253 |
| 8 | Chinese Academy of Sciences | 230 |
| 9 | Honda | 197 |
| 10 | Murata | 165 |

Group-level view changes the picture. Samsung SDI plus Samsung Electronics together exceed Toyota. Hyundai plus Kia, including a second Kia name cluster, also top 600. These are harmonized name clusters, so exact group totals carry some uncertainty.

**Polymer solid electrolytes (CPC H01M10/0565, 10,609 families)** is a different race. LG Energy Solution and LG Chem dominate, with their combined name clusters near 900 families. The Chinese Academy of Sciences ranks third, and Chinese universities and CATL are prominent. Toyota and Panasonic fall well down the list here.

**Geography and momentum**
- Ownership sits in Japan and Korea. Japanese applicants hold about 3,900 inorganic families and Korean applicants about 2,500, versus about 1,500 for the US and under 400 for China.
- China is nonetheless the largest filing office, ahead of the US, meaning foreign incumbents are filing defensively there.
- Filings in the inorganic class grew roughly tenfold from 2015 to 2023. The 2024 and 2025 dips are publication lag, not decline.
- Notable recent entrants since 2021 include SK On, POSCO Holdings, Geely and several Chinese startups. Chinese players are entering fast but have not yet displaced the Japanese and Korean incumbents in family counts.

**Caveat on scope.** Startups like QuantumScape and Solid Power do not appear in the top 15 by volume, though QuantumScape's garnet family from 2013 is among the most-cited in the field. Volume leadership and technical influence are not the same thing.
